purpose: Voxelotor is used to treat sickle cell disease in adults and children 4 years and older. It helps reduce the breakdown of red blood cells that happens because of this condition. By doing this, it can help improve anemia and reduce some of the complications of sickle cell disease.
how_it_works: In sickle cell disease, red blood cells contain an abnormal hemoglobin that causes them to clump together and form a sickle shape, which damages the cells. Voxelotor works by attaching to this abnormal hemoglobin and helping it hold onto oxygen better. This keeps the red blood cells from clumping and changing into that harmful sickle shape.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, rash, tiredness, and fever. Some people may also notice their skin or eyes look slightly yellow, which should be reported to your doctor right away.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any liver problems, as voxelotor can sometimes affect the liver. It can also interact with certain other medications, especially ones that affect liver enzymes, so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist or doctor. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. Seek medical help right away if you develop signs of a serious allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, or severe rash.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults and children 12 years and older is 1,500 mg (three 500 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day with or without food. For children aged 4 to under 12, the dose is based on weight and determined by the doctor. Try to take it at the same time each day, and swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them.
